_readme: GOLDEN SET for the ReliefWeb figure extractor (Phase 3 acceptance).
Ten documents modelled on real ReliefWeb reporting for a March 2024
flood in the Philippines, each paired with the model response it should
produce and with what the deterministic post-processing must then do
with it. Bodies are shortened but every `quote` below appears in its
document VERBATIM — that is the property the extractor's quote verifier
checks, so a fixture that got it wrong would fail the suite rather than
The set deliberately covers the awkward cases: a document that states no
qualifying figure at all, a figure given in households, a cumulative
figure, a figure repeated verbatim across two reports, a figure larger
than modelled exposure, a quote the document does not contain, and a
report that breaks one event into per-province figures that must not be
`expected` is what parse_response must return for that document;
`expected_rejected` lists the reasons it must report.

doc.title: Philippines: Floods - Situation Report No. 3
doc.body:
PHILIPPINES: FLOODS
Situation Report No. 3

Heavy monsoon rains continued across Luzon this week. OCHA reports that 145,000 people have been affected across four provinces as of 13 March 2024. Response operations are ongoing and 12 evacuation centres remain open. Damage to agriculture is still being assessed.

doc.title: NDRRMC Situational Report for Southwest Monsoon
doc.body:
NATIONAL DISASTER RISK REDUCTION AND MANAGEMENT COUNCIL
Situational Report No. 12

The NDRRMC reports a total of 152,340 persons affected in Regions III and IV-A as of 18 March 2024. A total of 31 deaths have been confirmed. Assistance amounting to PHP 42 million has been provided to affected families.

sources: International Federation of Red Cross And Red Crescent Societies
doc.body:
OPERATIONAL UPDATE

The Philippine Red Cross reports that 30,000 households have been affected by flooding in the worst-hit municipalities. Volunteers have distributed hygiene kits and hot meals. Water levels have begun to recede in low-lying areas.

doc.title: Philippines flooding: damage assessment note
doc.body:
DAMAGE ASSESSMENT NOTE

Initial assessments indicate that 1,240 houses were totally damaged and 3,800 partially damaged. Eleven people were killed and four remain missing. Road access to three municipalities is cut. No consolidated figure for people affected is available at this time.

doc.title: Philippines: Floods - Situation Report No. 5
doc.body:
PHILIPPINES: FLOODS
Situation Report No. 5

A cumulative total of 210,000 people have been affected since the onset of flooding on 3 March 2024. The figure includes populations affected in earlier phases of the emergency. Humanitarian partners continue to scale up the response.

doc.body:
PROVINCIAL REPORTS

The provincial government of Rizal reports 12,000 people affected. In Bulacan, the provincial disaster office reports 8,500 people affected. The provincial government of Pampanga reports 21,300 people affected. Consolidation at national level is pending.
